_comment: Packs for the il / lo / la / l' trainer (/articles), see src/lib/artikelPacks.js. `topics` groups the lexicon's own unit topics (src/content/lexicon/*.json; the topic ids stayed German) into everyday packs; a noun belongs to the pack of its FIRST topic, so every tagged noun is in exactly one. `rules` are patterns of the noun's first word, checked in this order. A rule with `genus` (m or f) is a GENDER rule: a noun joins it when its gender matches (l'amica is feminine, whichever article it takes); nouns that match the pattern and break it are the exceptions (la mano, il pianeta). A rule with `starts` (a regex) is a SOUND rule: l' before a vowel, lo before z-, s+consonant, gn-, ps-; `onlyGenus` keeps the other gender out (la zia is not a lo word); sound rules have no exceptions. `names` is a word list, `suffixes` are endings, `why` names the pattern in the explanation. `min` lowers minPack for a rule with few nouns. `noRule` lists set phrases no rule speaks about; acronyms are skipped by the code. The rules are general teaching rules for standard Italian (variety it-IT), not taken from any exam material.
_levels: A topic pack's `levels` renames it per level: one lexicon topic holds different nouns at each level (A1 wohnen = kitchen, bathroom; A2 = deposit, landlord), so no pack name repeats across A1–B2. `name`/`icon` are the fallback.

rules.name: Vowel: l'
rules.rule: Before a vowel, il, lo and la all become l', for masculine and feminine alike: l'amico, l'amica, l'uomo, l'acqua, l'ospedale. So l' does not tell you the gender: the plural does (gli amici, le amiche).
rules.ruleLeicht: The word starts with a vowel (a, e, i, o, u)? Then you say “l'”: l'amico, l'amica.

rules.name: z, s + consonant, gn, ps: lo
rules.rule: Masculine nouns that start with z, s + consonant, gn or ps (also x and y) take lo, not il: lo zaino, lo studente, lo straniero, lo psicologo. The plural is gli: gli zaini, gli studenti.
rules.ruleLeicht: A masculine word with z-, s + consonant (sp-, st-, sc-…), gn- or ps-? Then you say “lo”: lo zaino, lo studente.

rules.name: -zione and -sione
rules.rule: Nouns in -zione and -sione are feminine: la stazione, la lezione, la televisione, la decisione. The plural is le: le stazioni.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -zione or -sione? Then you say “la”: la stazione.

rules.name: -tà and -tù
rules.rule: Nouns in -tà and -tù are feminine and do not change in the plural: la città, la verità, la qualità, la gioventù; le città.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -tà or -tù? Then you say “la”: la città.

rules.name: -si (from Greek)
rules.rule: Nouns in -si from Greek are feminine and do not change in the plural: la crisi, la tesi, l'analisi, l'ipotesi, la diagnosi; le crisi.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -si? Then you say “la” (or “l'” before a vowel): la crisi, la tesi.

rules.name: -ma words from Greek
rules.rule: Many words in -ma come from Greek and are masculine: il problema, il tema, il sistema, il programma, il clima. Not every word in -ma: la mamma, la forma, la crema, la gamma.
rules.ruleLeicht: These words end in -ma, but you say “il”: il problema, il tema.

rules.name: -ore
rules.rule: Most nouns in -ore are masculine: il colore, il dolore, il fiore, il motore, il calore, il valore. Words for people in -tore follow: il direttore, il lavoratore (the feminine is -trice: la direttrice).
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -ore? Then you usually say “il”: il colore, il fiore.

rules.name: -ie
rules.rule: Nouns in -ie are feminine and do not change in the plural: la serie, la specie, la superficie; le serie.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -ie? Then you say “la”: la serie, la specie.

rules.name: -o
rules.rule: Most nouns in -o are masculine: il libro, il lavoro, il vaso, lo zaino. The ones to watch: la mano, la foto, la moto, la radio. The plural is -i: i libri.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -o? Then you usually say “il” (or “lo”): il libro.

rules.name: -a
rules.rule: Most nouns in -a are feminine: la casa, la sedia, la tavola, l'amica. The ones to watch: il pianeta, il papa, il poeta, il cinema (and the -ma words from Greek). The plural is -e: le case.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -a? Then you usually say “la”: la casa.
